scenario.description: A Director of Engineering must decide whether to approve publication of an internal developer CLI as an open-source project, setting its release scope, telemetry behavior, dependency remediation, and maintenance model after the normal release-readiness review.

shared_context.S1: The internal developer CLI has been used by the engineering organization for six months and is proposed for publication in the company's public code repository next week.
shared_context.S2: Morgan has authority to approve or reject the public release plan.
shared_context.S3: The CLI's standard functional tests and automated security scan passed, and the draft release plan proposes publishing the complete current repository with telemetry enabled.
shared_context.S4: The release-readiness meeting follows the team's normal practice of hearing a specific review from developer tools, security, developer relations, and engineering operations before Morgan records the final plan. The release plan template records each required remediation as a separate commitment using the exact commitment types dependency_removal, telemetry_disablement, private_plugin_exclusion, and public_maintainer_triage, and records the corresponding decision fields using their exact enum or numeric values.

PF1.text: While preparing the packaging script for a different task yesterday, Ravi found that the repository bundles a parser library under the AGPL-3.0 license, which cannot be distributed in this project under the company's approved open-source terms; he has not filed the packaging issue yet because he was waiting to confirm the library's embedded version.

PF2.text: Elise confirmed this morning by inspecting a runtime trace that the CLI sends repository names and branch names to the company's hosted telemetry endpoint; public distribution requires telemetry to be off by default, although the standard security scan did not exercise that runtime path, and she has not added the finding to the release ticket yet.

PF3.text: Jonah's partner review shows that the Northstar SSO plugin and Kestrel billing plugin are proprietary extensions used by external pilot teams, so both plugin packages must be excluded from the public repository while the core CLI can still be published; he found this in the partner-access list during another review and has not updated the release draft.

PF4.text: Tessa's current ownership roster has no maintained support rotation for a public project; the operations policy requires exactly two named maintainers and a recurring triage commitment before an internal tool is published, and she confirmed the roster gap while preparing next month's staffing report but has not raised it in the release channel.

acceptance_conditions: The public release must remain unapproved until the four required remediations are completed.
The AGPL parser dependency removal must be required in the release plan.
Telemetry must be recorded as off_by_default.
The Northstar SSO plugin and Kestrel billing plugin must be excluded from the public repository.
Exactly two named maintainers must be assigned.
Ravi's licensing finding must be cited as justification after Ravi states it.

decisive_facts.why: The clean automated checks leave no known licensing remediation; PF1 changes the plan to require removal or replacement of the AGPL-3.0 parser and adds a dependency_removal commitment.
The draft enables telemetry; PF2 changes the exact telemetry_mode value to off_by_default and adds a telemetry_disablement commitment.
The draft publishes the complete repository; PF3 changes the exact excluded_private_plugins list to Northstar SSO plugin and Kestrel billing plugin and adds a private_plugin_exclusion commitment.
The draft has no public maintenance assignment; PF4 changes named_maintainer_count to exactly 2 and adds a public_maintainer_triage commitment.
